paper.title: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties
paper.venue: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

problem_tree.node: Root: Development of a machine learning framework for predicting material properties from crystal structures
problem_tree.description: The paper presents a crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) framework that learns material properties directly from the atomic connectivity in crystal structures, aiming for both accuracy and interpretability.
problem_tree.evidence: The abstract and introduction discuss the need for a new method to predict material properties accurately and interpretably.

children.node: RQ1: How accurately can the CGCNN predict various material properties compared to DFT calculations?
children.description: This question investigates the predictive performance of the CGCNN framework against established DFT calculations for different material properties.
children.evidence: The results section and Table I summarize the prediction performance of the CGCNN for various properties.

children.task: Predict formation energy per atom using CGCNN
dataset: Materials Project database with 28046 training data points
children.protocol_or_setup: Training with 60% of data, validation with 20%, and testing with 20%
children.conclusion: The CGCNN achieves a MAE of 0.039 eV/atom for formation energy, demonstrating high accuracy.

children.task: Predict other material properties (absolute energy, band gap, etc.) using CGCNN
dataset: Materials Project database with various training data points for each property
metrics: MAE for absolute energy: 0.072 eV/atom, band gap: 0.388 eV
children.protocol_or_setup: Similar training and validation setup as above
children.conclusion: The CGCNN provides reliable predictions for multiple properties, with MAEs close to DFT accuracy.

children.node: RQ2: How does the CGCNN framework provide interpretability in material property predictions?
children.description: This question explores how the CGCNN allows for the extraction of local chemical environment contributions to global properties.
children.evidence: The discussion section highlights the interpretability aspect of the CGCNN framework.

children.task: Extract site energies in perovskites from total energy above hull
metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.130 eV/atom for site energy predictions
children.protocol_or_setup: Using total energy above hull data for training
children.conclusion: The CGCNN allows for the extraction of site-specific energies, providing insights into material stability.

children.node: RQ3: What are the implications of the CGCNN framework for materials design and discovery?
children.description: This question assesses how the insights gained from the CGCNN can guide the design of new materials, particularly perovskites.
children.evidence: The conclusion discusses the potential for high-throughput screening and materials discovery.

children.task: Identify potentially synthesizable perovskites using CGCNN insights
dataset: 378 perovskite candidates with energies above hull < 0.2 eV/atom
model_or_method: Combinational search based on CGCNN predictions
children.protocol_or_setup: Using insights from site energy predictions to guide searches
children.conclusion: The CGCNN framework significantly reduces the search space for new materials, enhancing discovery efficiency.
